explore-current.title: Build it, then push some current
explore-current.prompt: Drag the battery, the resistor and the ammeter onto the breadboard. Close the switch, then turn up the battery until the ammeter reads 0.2 A.
hints: The battery goes on the left, the resistor on the right. The ammeter fills the gap at the top so current can flow through it.
Current needs a complete loop. Close the switch.
Each volt pushes 1/30 of an ampere through 30 Ω. How many volts make 0.2 A?
explore-current.success: 6 volts pushes 0.2 amperes through 30 ohms. More voltage, more current.

explore-resistance.title: Hold the current back
explore-resistance.prompt: The battery is fixed at 12 V. Change the resistor until the ammeter reads 0.25 A.
hints: Right now the current is too small. Less resistance lets more current through.
You need a resistor that lets exactly a quarter of an ampere through from 12 V.
explore-resistance.success: 48 ohms lets 0.25 amperes flow from 12 volts. More resistance, less current.

explore-voltage.title: How much push?
explore-voltage.prompt: Set the resistor to 2 Ω, then find the battery voltage that pushes exactly 0.5 A through it.
hints: Drag the resistor all the way down to 2 Ω first.
With 2 Ω, every volt pushes half an ampere.

predict-double.title: Double the resistance
predict-double.prompt: Same 12 V battery, but the 48 Ω resistor has been swapped for 96 Ω.

sandbox.title: Check any number
sandbox.prompt: Type any voltage and resistance, including prefixes like 10m or 2.2k, and read the current and power.
